clue.text: Scotsman has friends in France confined in hotels

amis is French for friends

explanation.surface: A Scottish man with French friends who are stuck inside hotel rooms.
explanation.walkthrough: The French friends go between the two Hs: H(AMIS)H.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamish is a traditional Scottish first name, so it stands as an example of a man from Scotland.

clue.text: Top primate sitting on value that's unknown

explanation.definitionFit: The apex is the highest point or summit of something, a noun synonym for the top.

clue.text: Its disturbing when virtue and sin are confused

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A moral reflection: it is troubling when people cannot tell good from evil.

clue.text: Head is red, so occasionally needs such styling

explanation.definitionFit: A hairdo is the way a person's hair has been cut and arranged, which is styling of the head.

clue.text: Country person bearing some twisted longing for family again

taken as written before being jumbled

explanation.surface: A rural person with a warped desire to see their relatives once more.
explanation.walkthrough: A hick is American and British slang for a yokel; 'Country person' looks like a nationality but means someone from the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Homesick describes pining for home and the people there, so it means missing your relatives and wanting to be back.

clue.text: Going off over key lessees sounding difficult to please

indicators.note: in a down entry, over means placed above, so the first piece comes before the second
sounding means as heard when said, so the word is replaced by one pronounced the same

key in the sense of chief or principal

explanation.surface: Rotting goods sit above key tenants who are complaining loudly.
explanation.definitionFit: A high-maintenance person demands constant attention and is hard to satisfy, an idiom for a fussy, demanding character.

clue.text: US claims special treatment for Chicago and Oklahoma!

indicators.note: giving words special treatment means working them over, so their letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: America insists that two of its cities and states deserve favoured status.
explanation.walkthrough: Chicago and Oklahoma! look like a city and a state, but the exclamation mark gives away the stage show title.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicago and Oklahoma! are both famous stage shows with songs, so they are examples of the theatrical genre.

clue.text: Country has open society rising?

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means read from bottom to top, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: an airy room is open and spacious
S is the standard abbreviation for society

explanation.surface: A question of whether a nation's open society is on the rise.
explanation.definitionFit: Syria is a nation in the Middle East, an example of a sovereign state.

clue.text: Against cutting sharp supporting beam

clue.text: Support item during early development stage  …

blocks.note: a tee supports a golf ball
an item is a thing

explanation.surface: A supporting object used during a project's opening phase, running on into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Teething is when a baby's first teeth come through, and teething troubles are problems in any project's opening phase.

clue.text: …  bound to be over by June

definitions.note: describes the season rather than naming it

blocks.note: first meaning: a leap or jump
second meaning: the season that ends as June brings summer

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: certain to be finished by midsummer.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links it to the clue before, so 'bound to be over' reads as one phrase; split it after 'bound'. In the northern hemisphere the season runs March to May.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb or noun for leaping, and also the season before summer, which finishes once June arrives.

clue.text: Armed count gone mad in charge, becoming totalitarian

indicators.note: words that have gone mad are wildly disordered, so their letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written before being jumbled
IC is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.definitionFit: A totalitarian regime allows no opposition or free elections, so it is the opposite of a government chosen by the people.

clue.text: Introductions are commonly shorter without it

explanation.walkthrough: Presenters say 'without further ado' before introducing someone, so the phrase itself literally makes introductions shorter.
explanation.definitionFit: Further ado means additional fuss or delay, which is exactly what a brisk introduction does without.

clue.text: Popular poet starts to rhapsodise using mystical imagery

indicators.note: starts means the opening letters, so only the first letter of each following word is kept

blocks.note: the initial letters of these four words

explanation.surface: A well-loved poet tends to rhapsodise in mystical images.
explanation.walkthrough: Rumi was a thirteenth-century Persian Sufi poet, now a bestseller in translation, so the surface also describes him.
explanation.definitionFit: Rumi is among the most widely read poets in the world today, a fitting example of a much-loved verse writer.

clue.text: Cuban perhaps getting ground into endless misery

one word going into another is put inside it

blocks.note: ground in the sense of terrain
taken as written before losing its ends

explanation.surface: A Cuban being pushed down into unending wretchedness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cuban' tempts you toward cigars or nationality words; the definition rests on Cuba being an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuba is an island nation, so any Cuban is an example of an inhabitant of an island.

clue.text: Get snorer treated; you won't be sorry

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice to a partner: get the snorer medical help and you'll be glad you did.
explanation.definitionFit: Having nothing to feel remorse about is the state of mind you have when you will feel no repentance later.

clue.text: Spooner's happy supporter works on water

definitions.note: a verb phrase describing the person who does the job

clue.text: Play double set to capture record? That's most expensive

explanation.walkthrough: An EP, or extended play, is a record longer than a single but shorter than an album.
explanation.definitionFit: Steep is informal for overpriced, so its superlative describes whatever costs the highest amount.

clue.text: Lamented disrespectful daughter moving east

blocks.note: rude means disrespectful
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: Parents grieved over a cheeky daughter who has moved out east.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the D out of RUDE and put it on the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To rue is to regret bitterly, so its past tense means grieved over or regretted.

clue.text: More slick, having previously spoken in the Bronx?

explanation.walkthrough: The old New York accent famously says 'toity-toid street' for thirty-third street, so earlier becomes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Slick can mean greasy or covered in oil, so a slicker surface is a greasier, more lubricated one.

clue.text: It's painful to pick up when hot

hot in the sense of currently popular

explanation.definitionFit: Heart-rending things cause great sorrow and distress, so they are emotionally hurtful to witness.
